key_idea: Tao's slice-rank version of the Croot–Lev–Pach / Ellenberg–Gijswijt method: a cap set makes δ_0(x+y+z) on A³ a diagonal tensor of full slice rank |A|, but the low-degree polynomial expansion of δ_0(x+y+z) forces slice rank at most 3N.
reason: A short, two-lemma argument settles a famous problem by comparing two ways of measuring the same tensor. The diagonal lemma and the degree-pigeonhole step are each nearly trivial, so nothing in the proof is wasted. It is a true book proof, docked slightly only because the reason the polynomial degree bound wins is felt more than fully explained.
recognized: Ellenberg–Gijswijt cap set bound via Croot–Lev–Pach polynomial method, in Tao's symmetric slice-rank formulation (2016 blog post)
